title: A Dynamical Spacetime Hypothesis for Quantum Entanglement with a Proposed Experimental Test
content: Quantum entanglement is a central resource of quantum information science, yet its correlations are ordinarily treated as properties of the quantum state rather than as the outcome of an underlying physical process. Here we explore the hypothesis that these correlations are mediated dynamically by a field propagating locally at finite velocity through an extension of ordinary spacetime,  extending the kinematic proposal of Physical Review Research 7, 013261 (2025) to a constrained bulk-field dynamics. Motivated by the constraints imposed by no-signaling on finite-speed hidden-influence models, we consider a warped five-dimensional spacetime with an additional timelike coordinate. We show that the five-dimensional Einstein equations determine the warp factor within a symmetric ansatz, requiring a positive bulk cosmological constant. We show that null trajectories propagating through the additional timelike dimension can project onto arbitrarily large spatial distances at the same ordinary time, although these trajectories do not themselves connect separated points on the brane. Spectral analysis of a minimally coupled bulk scalar reveals a tachyonic four-dimensional continuum. We isolate a normalizable zero-mode sector with stable, retarded effective dynamics in ordinary brane time and obtain an exact solution for a suitably distributed source. Building on these results, we formulate an equal-time contextual coupling and Bohm–Bub-inspired outcome dynamics as additional hypotheses, subject to Born-rule compatibility and multipartite no-signaling. We propose an experiment involving two independently prepared Bell pairs to test for departures from their expected statistical independence. Under specified assumptions on the field covariance and detector response, we derive a conditional inverse-square decay of correlations between the two pairs' joint measurement outcomes at large separations. Whether such correlations are nonzero, and whether the complete dynamics reproduces Bell-inequality violations while preserving no-signaling and stability, remain open questions.
